newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel barges firm on low supply, short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel barges firm on low supply, short-covering.

text.p: European high sulphur barges firmed to two-month highs on Friday with market players blaming low regional supply.
After Thursday's strong showing business began at $86.75 a tonne before gaining in quarter dollar increments to $87.75, a level not seen since mid-March.
Opinions differed on the sustainability of the rise, given fuel oil is traditionally weak in the summer, and on how much of the rise was manipulative or the result of supply shortages.
"We'll definitely be firm for the next few days, as we know we are short material up to the 15th," said one trader.
"It's short-covering which is doing this, not the bunkers, and there is a bit of game playing going on," said another trader, "and it can be played because its very thin."
Large volumes of fuel oil were reported to have left NWE for the U.S. Atlantic Coast recently, or to fill the holes left in Med supply by arbitraging out to the Far East.
One Russian cracked cargo believed being chased by multiple buyers was heard moved to Spain to cover the traders short there.
